# prints a table to ensure more lines shown 
print.me <- function(x, ...) {
if (nrow(x) > 200){
   len <- 200 
    } else {
       len <- (nrow(x))
}
   x[1:len,] %>%
   kbl(digits=2, align= 'l', booktabs=T) %>%
   kable_styling(fixed_thead = T) %>%
   kable_paper("striped", full_width = T, html_font = "Merriweather", font_size = 12) %>%
   row_spec(0, color = "white", background = "#b07946", font_size = 12) %>%
   scroll_box(width = "737px", height = "200px") %>%
   asis_output()
}

registerS3method("knit_print", "data.frame", print.me)

Cleaning Genie

emma_genie <- function(input, text_col = NULL, replacements = T, omit_stops = T, lemmatize = T) {
  # load in necessary libraries for the cleaning genie function
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(stringr)
  library(stringi)
  
  # different input types
  if(is.character(input) & is.null(text_col)) {
    df <- data.frame(text = input, stringsAsFactors = F)
    text_col <- "text"
  } else if (is.data.frame(input)) {
    df <- input
    if (is.null(text_col)) stop(paste("Provide text_col when input is a dataframe."))
    } else {
      stop(paste("Input must be a character vector or a dataframe"))
    }

  # if the column specified by "wordcol" does not exist in "df", show an error message
  if (!text_col %in% names(df)) {
    stop(paste("Column", text_col, "not found in dataframe"))
  }
  
  # load contraction & stop word corpora
  load(url("https://github.com/Reilly-ConceptsCognitionLab/reillylab_publicdata/blob/main/Temple_stops25.rda?raw=true"))
  load(url("https://github.com/Reilly-ConceptsCognitionLab/reillylab_publicdata/blob/main/replacements_25.rda?raw=true"))
  
  # creates an ID column, selects text column from text_col, forces it into a character, fixes any encoding issues, converts it to UTF-8, and changes all text to lowercase
  prep <- df |>
    mutate(
      ID = factor(seq_len(nrow(df))),
      
      initial_split = tryCatch(
        stri_enc_toutf8(
          as.character(.data[[text_col]]),
          is_unknown_8bit = T,
          validate = T
          ),
        error = function(e) {
          stri_encode(
            as.character(.data[[text_col]]), 
            to = "UTF-8"
            )
          }
        ) |> tolower()
      )
 
  # preserve NA values and standardize apostrophes to the ASCII apostrophe to ensure that code doesn't break further down the pipeline because of variance in apostrophe types
   prep <- prep |>
    mutate(
      initial_split = ifelse(
      is.na(initial_split), 
      NA_character_, 
      stri_replace_all_regex(initial_split, "[\u2018\u2019\u02BC\u201B\uFF07\u0092\u0091\u0060\u00B4\u2032\u2035]", "'")
      )
    )
   
   # splits text into individual tokens by word and puts them in row format, converts blank tokens to NA, removes the original text column (in left to right format)
   prep <- prep |>
     separate_rows(initial_split, sep = "[[:space:]]+") |>
     
     mutate(
       initial_split = ifelse(
       is.na(initial_split) | stri_isempty(initial_split), 
       NA_character_, 
       initial_split)
       ) |>
     
     select(-all_of(text_col))
   
   # PIECE OF GENIE THAT WILL BE EDITED BASED ON CLEANING NEEDS
   # removes punctuation, special characters, and whitespace. keeps apostrophes for contraction expansion purposes and hyphenated words to preserve their meaning.
   prep <- prep |>
     mutate(
       clean = initial_split,
       
       clean = ifelse(
         is.na(clean), 
         NA_character_, 
         stri_replace_all_regex(clean, "[^a-zA-Z0-9-']", "") 
         ),
       
       clean = ifelse(
         is.na(clean), 
         NA_character_, 
         str_squish(clean)
         ),
       
       clean = ifelse(
         is.na(clean), 
         NA_character_, 
         stri_replace_all_regex(clean, "[^a-z'-]", "")
         )
       )
   
   # expands contractions with keeping all other words and preserving NAs
   if(replacements) {
     map <- setNames(
       tolower(replacements_25$replacement),
       tolower(replacements_25$word)
     )
     
     prep <- prep |>
       mutate(
         clean = ifelse(
           is.na(clean),
           NA_character_,
           dplyr::recode(tolower(clean), !!!map, .default = clean)
         )
       )
   }
   
   # splits new clean version into tokens and forces individual words into rows; removes all apostrophes
   prep <- prep |>
     separate_rows(clean, sep = "[[:space:]]+", convert = T) |>
     mutate(
       clean = ifelse(
         is.na(clean) | stri_isempty(clean),
         NA_character_,
         stri_replace_all_regex(clean, "'", "")
       ),
       ID_post_split = seq_len(dplyr::n())
     )
   
   # lemmatizes words (basic dictionary form)
   if(lemmatize) {
     prep <- prep |>
       mutate(
         clean = ifelse(
           is.na(clean),
           NA_character_,
           textstem::lemmatize_strings(clean)
         )
       )
   }
   
   # removes stop words and flags where they were with NAs
   if (omit_stops) {
     stopwords <- tolower(Temple_stops25$word)
     
     prep <- prep |>
       mutate(
         is_stopword = ifelse(
           is.na(clean),
           NA,
           clean %in% stopwords
         ),
         clean = ifelse(
           is_stopword,
           NA_character_,
           clean
         )
       ) |>
       select(-is_stopword)
   }
   
   return(prep)
}

# clean df
clean <- emma_genie(df, text_col = "recall_text") |>
  rename(word = clean)

Data Configuration and Cleaning

# merge the new cleaned data with the lookup database
clean <- clean |>
    left_join(lookup_Jul25, by = "word") |>
    select(PID, SceneID, word, sem_cnc_v2013_rescale, sem_visual_rescale) |>
    drop_na() |>
    group_by(PID, SceneID) |>
    mutate(concrete_avg = mean(sem_cnc_v2013_rescale), visual_avg = mean(sem_visual_rescale))

# merge cleaned data with the full dataframe for EmoNet variables
stimulus <- clean |>
    left_join(full, by = c("PID", "SceneID")) |>
    select(-avg_uncert, -recall_text)

# merge cleaned data with full dataframe for average uncertainty variable
participant <- clean |>
    left_join(full, by = c("PID", "SceneID")) |>
    select(-(Adoration:Surprise)) |>
    drop_na()

Analyses

Stimulus-driven emotion analysis:

# hypothesis model
ha <- lmer(concrete_avg ~ Disgust + Surprise + Sadness + Joy + (1 | PID), data = stimulus)
summary(ha)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method [
## lmerModLmerTest]
## Formula: concrete_avg ~ Disgust + Surprise + Sadness + Joy + (1 | PID)
##    Data: stimulus
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: 24047.4
## 
## Scaled residuals:

## -4.1251 -0.6429 -0.0755  0.5100  7.7989 
## 
## Random effects:

##  PID      (Intercept) 0.07126  0.2669

## Number of obs: 18904, groups:  PID, 32
## 
## Fixed effects:

## Surprise     1.462e+00  1.968e-01  1.889e+04   7.431 1.13e-13 ***

## Joy          6.075e-01  8.666e-02  1.887e+04   7.011 2.45e-12 ***
## ---

Plots

Stimulus-driven emotion analysis:

stimulus |>
    ggplot(aes(x = Disgust, y = concrete_avg)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm",
    color = colors[1]) + labs(x = "Average Disgust per Scene", y = "Average Concreteness") +
    theme_minimal()

stimulus |>
    ggplot(aes(x = Disgust, y = visual_avg)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm",
    color = colors[1]) + labs(x = "Average Disgust per Scene", y = "Average Visual Salience") +
    theme_minimal()

Participant-driven emotion analysis:

participant |>
    ggplot(aes(x = avg_uncert, y = concrete_avg)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ poly(x, 2), se = TRUE, color = colors[3]) + labs(x = "Average Uncertainty",
    y = "Average Concreteness") + theme_minimal()

participant |>
    ggplot(aes(x = avg_uncert, y = visual_avg)) + geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ poly(x, 2), se = TRUE, color = colors[3]) + labs(x = "Average Uncertainty",
    y = "Average Visual Salience") + theme_minimal()
